title: PensionHunter: Find Lost Pensions Abroad in 41 Countries
excerpt: Worked abroad? Free check shows which countries may hold a pension in your name. Researched reports from $99, full refund if we find nothing material.
content_html:
Building the world's pension identification infrastructure

Find the pensions you left abroad

Your state and workplace pensions, traced from official sources. Free check in 41 countries.

You can add more countries on the next step.

41 countries · 24 languages · official sources only

How it works

  1. Tick the countries you worked in.
  2. We find who holds each pension today, your state pension and your workplace pensions, from official sources, even where an employer was renamed or merged.
  3. You get one full, clear report and contact them yourself.

Schemes do not lose the money. They lose the person. You move on, then you move house. The scheme writes to an old address, and the employer is bought, renamed or wound up. Read why

Among the countries we research: United Kingdom, United States, Netherlands, Ireland, Germany, Switzerland, Canada, New Zealand, South Africa. See every country we cover

Try the official route first. Many countries run their own government service to trace a pension or show what you have built up. Where a country's route is genuinely free and open from abroad, we say so and point you straight to it. See the official routes by country

Three ways to start

  • Free check

    See what may be waiting.

    Start the free check

  • Order a report, from $99

    We name who holds it.

    See the three reports

  • Free pension register

    Funds find you as they join.

    Register free

Free pension register

GPFR is a free pension register for people who worked abroad: you add yourself once. As pension funds join, they check GPFR for former members they cannot reach. Nothing is shared without your yes, and funds pay us per confirmed match, never you. Matching starts as funds join.

Register free

Every fact sourced and dated

Every statement in a report carries a source and a date, so it can be handed to a lawyer, filed with a will, and acted on by your family without you in the room.

Each finding names the source we used and the date we read it. We work from official registers and national tracing routes, published scheme and administrator directories, employer records, and our own dated correspondence with national authorities.

Every report names the free official route first. A human researcher reviews every report before it is sent. Where a detail cannot be verified, it is left out and the gap is stated.

We write to most pension authorities in the countries we cover, stay in contact with them and update our facts as they answer. Read their written answers

Why people trust us

Advanced research technology, checked by people. A named researcher reads every report.

PensionHunter is not regulated by the FCA. We identify pensions and do not give advice.

Identification and research only. No advice, no commission, we never hold your money.

Security pledge: what we never ask you forAbout PensionHunter

Who is behind PensionHunter

Frank Marco

Founder

Read the founder's story

Questions

What do I get for $99?

Who holds each of your pensions today, state and workplace, including employers that were renamed or merged, with the official contact route and any deadlines. One full report in 24 to 48 hours, read by a named researcher.

See a full sample report

My old employer no longer exists or changed its name. Can you still find my pension?

Yes, that is what we specialise in. We trace your old employer to the fund or insurer that holds your pension today and give you the official route to contact them.

Is this legitimate, and do you take a cut of my pension?

We are a UK company (No. 13326151), ICO registered (ZC113586), rated on Trustpilot. You pay a fixed price, we never take a commission and we never touch your money.

What if you find nothing?

You pay up front. If our report does not name who holds a pension in your name, or give you a verified route to your own record beyond a free register check, we refund you in full.

What is the free pension register?

It is free for you: pension funds look for former members there as they join. Nothing is shared without your yes.
